comparisons.peer_topic: Redemption Rights and Depositary Share Structures
comparisons.peer_summary: The Corporation may redeem most preferred stock series at its option at liquidation preference plus unpaid dividends, except for Series B and Series L which lack early redemption rights. Ownership is generally held via depositary shares representing fractional interests in preferred stock, with dividend payment frequencies and minimum rates varying by series as detailed in the table footnotes.
comparisons.comparison: Citi and BAC both utilize depositary shares to represent fractional interests in their non-cumulative perpetual preferred stock, though the fraction sizes differ. Citi's Series EE uses a 1/25th interest structure with quarterly dividends that reset to the five-year treasury rate plus 2.572% after February 15, 2030. BAC also issues depositary shares (variously 1/25th, 1/1000th, etc.) with quarterly dividends when declared, but its disclosures highlight general redemption rights at liquidation preference plus unpaid dividends, whereas Citi's specific disclosure focuses on the dividend reset mechanics and declaration status.

sentences.text: (16)Issued as depositary shares, each representing a 1/25th interest in a share of the corresponding series of non-cumulative perpetual preferred stock.

Dividends are payable quarterly on February 15, May 15, August 15 and November 15 at a fixed rate until, but excluding, February 15, 2030, thereafter payable quarterly on the same dates at a fixed rate that resets on the Series EE reset date and every five years thereafter equal to the five-year treasury rate plus 2.572%, in each case when, as and if declared by the Citi Board of Directors.

(6)Ownership is held in the form of depositary shares, each representing a 1/25th interest in a share of preferred stock, paying a semi-annual cash dividend, if and when declared, until the first redemption date at which time, it adjusts to a quarterly cash dividend, if and when declared, thereafter.
(2)The Corporation may redeem series of preferred stock on or after the redemption date, in whole or in part, at its option, at the liquidation preference plus declared and unpaid dividends.

comparisons.peer_topic: 2025 Issuance of Series Z Preferred Stock
comparisons.peer_summary: In January 2025, the firm issued 76,000 shares of Series Z 6.85% Fixed-Rate Reset Non-Cumulative Preferred Stock, which has a $25,000 liquidation preference, is redeemable at the firm's option starting February 10, 2030, and pays semi-annual dividends at 6.85% per annum until that date, thereafter resetting to 2.461% plus the five-year treasury rate.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Goldman Sachs issue fixed-rate reset non-cumulative preferred stock with dividends payable until a specific reset date linked to Treasury rates. Citi's Series EE pays quarterly dividends at a fixed rate until February 15, 2030, then resets to the five-year treasury rate plus 2.572%. Similarly, Goldman's Series Z, issued in January 2025, pays semi-annual dividends at 6.85% until February 10, 2030, then resets to the five-year treasury rate plus 2.461%. Both instruments are redeemable at the company's option at their respective reset dates.

sentences.text: Dividends are payable quarterly on February 15, May 15, August 15 and November 15 at a fixed rate until, but excluding, February 15, 2030, thereafter payable quarterly on the same dates at a fixed rate that resets on the Series EE reset date and every five years thereafter equal to the five-year treasury rate plus 2.572%, in each case when, as and if declared by the Citi Board of Directors.

Dividends on Series Z Preferred Stock, if declared, are payable semi-annually at (i) 6.85% per annum from the issuance date to, but excluding, February 10, 2030 and, thereafter, (ii) 2.461% per annum plus the five-year treasury rate.

Each share of Series Z Preferred Stock issued and outstanding has a liquidation preference of $25,000 per share, is represented by 25 depositary shares and is redeemable at the firm's option beginning February 10, 2030 at a redemption price equal to $25,000 per share plus declared and unpaid dividends.

comparisons.peer_topic: Preferred Stock Dividend Policy and Reference Rates
comparisons.peer_summary: Dividends are discretionary, non-cumulative, and declared quarterly. Fixed-to-floating rate preferred stock uses SOFR or CMT as reference rates following the transition from LIBOR, with specific spread adjustments defined.
comparisons.comparison: Citi and JPMorgan both disclose that preferred stock dividends are paid only when and as declared by the Board, characterizing them as non-cumulative. Citi specifies quarterly payments for Series EE. JPMorgan confirms that dividends on its non-cumulative preferred stock are declared quarterly (or semi-annually while at a fixed rate before conversion to floating), and explicitly notes that its fixed-to-floating rates use CMT (Constant Maturity Treasury) or SOFR, similar to Citi's reliance on the five-year treasury rate for resets.

Citi's Series EE pays quarterly dividends from issuance. Morgan Stanley's Series M pays semi-annually until September 15, 2026, and then quarterly. While the specific series differ, both disclosures highlight the contractual modification of dividend payment schedules over the life of the instrument.
